stem:
Aisha notices that ice cubes melt faster on a dark steel plate than on a white ceramic plate on the same sunny windowsill. This makes her ask new questions about colour, heat, and melting.

Which claim about her observation is correct?

options.text: Careful observations can answer one question and also open new questions that guide further exploration.
Even careless observations provide dependable evidence for deciding what to investigate next.
Observations count as evidence only when they agree with an explanation she already believes.
Watching ice melt on kitchen plates cannot start scientific exploration; only laboratory work can.

teacher.key_rationale: Careful observations can settle one question while opening new ones. Careless observations are not dependable evidence; evidence is not limited to confirming prior beliefs; everyday melting observations can start scientific exploration.
